In fitting a smoothing spline, we do not need to select the number or location of the knots—there will be a knot at each training observation, x1,⋯, xn. Instead, we have another problem: we need to choose the value of λ. It should come as no surprise that one possible solution to this problem is cross-validation. In other words, we can find the value of λ that makes the cross-validated RSS as small as possible.
